# Bernd Huber

> Research scientist in New York. Research in audio, language models, and learning from human preference. PhD in Computer Science, Harvard University.

## Selected work

- Reward modeling for music agents: developed an approach at Spotify combining reward models and direct preference optimization (DPO). Listening feedback on generated playlists informs optimization of tool-use plans. Production A/B tests reported 70% fewer erroneous tool calls and a 4% increase in listening time.
  https://research.atspotify.com/2025/9/personalizing-agentic-ai-to-users-musical-tastes-with-scalable-preference-optimization
- Embedding-to-Prefix (E2P): developed a method mapping existing user embeddings to a single learned soft prefix token for a frozen LLM. E2P was used for long-term personalization in GLIDE, Spotify's generative podcast recommender.
  https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.17051
  https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17540
- Conversational speech: developed SpecialTime for real-time dialogue-act feedback in parent–child speech, and Meeter for analyzing information sharing and shared understanding in group discussions. Co-authored work on real-time speech emotion recognition on mobile devices.
  https://doi.org/10.1145/3329189.3329203
  https://doi.org/10.1145/3359132
  https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/7344658
- Image-grounded dialogue generation: with Microsoft Research, developed dialogue models conditioned on visual sentiment, scene features, and facial expressions. Companion work studied facial-expression-grounded dialogue generation.
  https://doi.org/10.1145/3173574.3173851
  https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/8373852

## Other work

- Co-authored research on data selection for continual adaptation of generative recommenders.
  https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07739
- Developed B-Script at Adobe Research for transcript-based B-roll recommendations; related US Patent 11,049,525.
  https://doi.org/10.1145/3290605.3300311
  https://patents.google.com/patent/US11049525B2/en
- Harvard dissertation: Interactive AI to Support Human-Human Communication.
  https://dash.harvard.edu/entities/publication/60c725b7-a8cf-4713-91dc-808a6688b717
